methodology.displayName: Threshold funding and dominant-assurance causal methodology v2

estimandDefinitions.success_case_additional: Other eligible participant funding activated on success, excluding the focal pledge, unconditional baseline funding, refunds, duplicates, and platform-funded bonuses.
estimandDefinitions.expected_additional: The validated with-pledge versus without-pledge change in threshold-success probability multiplied by other eligible funding. It is withheld without an interference-aware causal design.
estimandDefinitions.direct_causal_attribution: The focal pledge's marginal effect under the validated pledge-arrival design, capped at other eligible funding and defaulting to non-additive across participants.
estimandDefinitions.verified_outcome: Eligible funding captured or externally verified after resolution, net of refunds and duplicates. This verifies funding occurrence, not the focal pledge's causal effect.
estimandDefinitions.cooperative_allocation: A non-additive Shapley allocation of coalition-created eligible funding under the frozen threshold ledger.
estimandDefinitions.platform_funded_bonus: A failure bonus or subsidy paid by Moral Trade or a sponsor, labeled separately and excluded from participant-caused totals.

methodology.baselineDefinition: Immediately before pledge exposure, freeze threshold, deadline, eligibility, supporter rule, ledger, funded amount, pledge, payment state, refund rules, failure-bonus design, and off-platform funding.

causalIdentificationPolicy.estimand: The causal estimand is the difference in threshold success and other eligible funding captured under the focal pledge's presence versus absence at the same pre-exposure pool state.
admissibleDesigns: randomized pledge invitation or reminder with noncompliance and spillover analysis
pre-specified discontinuity or randomized bonus-design arm with interference-aware analysis
causalIdentificationPolicy.interferencePolicy: Represent how the focal pledge changes later pledge arrivals, withdrawals, and payment behavior. Use an exposure mapping or cluster design; do not assume independent pledges.
causalIdentificationPolicy.overlapAndPositivityPolicy: Estimate causal effects only in states with empirical support for both the with-participant and without-participant conditions. Fail closed when overlap or positivity is materially violated.
causalIdentificationPolicy.sensitivityAnalysisPolicy: Report pre-specified sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounding, baseline misclassification, and interference. Withhold causal components when conclusions are not robust to the approved bounds.

evidenceSemanticsPolicy.publicCopyRule: Evidence may establish that an outcome occurred and its quantity. It must not be described as verified impact or verified additionality; causal additionality remains an assessed model output.

strategicBehaviorPolicy.baselineAntecedenceRule: A baseline can support additionality only when its material evidence predates the participant-facing offer or commitment and survives post-resolution consistency checks.
strategicBehaviorPolicy.strategicTimingRule: Freeze the ledger before exposure and detect pledge splitting, strategic delay, coordinated timing, and post-deadline edits.
strategicBehaviorPolicy.interferenceRule: Represent how the focal pledge changes later pledge arrivals, withdrawals, and payment behavior. Use an exposure mapping or cluster design; do not assume independent pledges.
strategicBehaviorPolicy.perverseIncentiveRule: Reject designs that reward manufactured shortfalls or threats; keep failure bonuses outside participant-caused accounting.

methodology.algorithmDescription: Compute deterministic other eligible funding. Predict threshold success and payment capture separately. Estimate with-pledge versus without-pledge effects only through a pre-specified interference-aware pledge-arrival design. Treat failure-bonus design as a treatment feature whose sign and magnitude require identification; never assume a beneficial response. Record captured funding and platform bonuses as separate outcomes.

referenceClassPolicy.uncertaintyExpansionRule: Reference classes support outcome prediction, not causal identification. Expand the 80% predictive interval at every approved broadening step and withhold when no defensible class remains.

uncertaintyPolicy.method: Use a pre-specified hierarchical predictive model and propagate parameter, outcome, baseline, interference, and measurement uncertainty by posterior or repeated-sampling simulation.
uncertaintyPolicy.confidencePolicy: The initial sample-size and calibration cutoffs are provisional governance floors. Low or moderate confidence may be shown only after a current health pass. High confidence is forbidden until temporal or otherwise independent holdout validation and uncertainty-aware calibration criteria are approved.

requiredBeforeHighConfidence: pre-registered temporal or otherwise independent holdout evaluation
uncertainty intervals for calibration intercept, slope, and interval coverage
documented robustness to approved confounding and interference sensitivity analyses

requiredCalibrationMetrics: out-of-sample probability calibration intercept and slope with uncertainty
out-of-sample Brier or proper scoring-rule result
blockedConditions: causal identification design is not validated
empirical calibration evidence is absent or ineligible
required state is missing or does not match the immutable state hash
input is outside the approved domain
unresolved evidence-integrity, duplication, or overlap failure
available modeled component would be published under blocked, warning, or stale health
warningConditions: reference class broadened beyond the narrowest approved class
material reliance on participant attestation rather than independent outcome evidence
calibration drift remains within a non-blocking warning band

sourceDataRequirements: immutable threshold, deadline, eligibility, refund, and bonus rules
participant-scoped pledge and payment ledger with deduplication keys
resolution, capture, refund, and external receipt evidence
separate platform or sponsor subsidy ledger
audited resolved threshold and dominant-assurance outcomes
knownFailureModes: predictive pledge-arrival model is treated as causal pivotality
strategic timing or pledge splitting changes other arrivals
duplicate or ineligible supporters inflate the ledger
bonus response is assumed positive without identification
platform bonus is mislabeled as participant impact
outOfDomainConditions: mutable threshold, deadline, or eligibility terms
private pool whose ledger cannot be audited
non-monetary threshold without a separate native-unit model
materialChangeTriggers: causal-identification design or sensitivity-analysis policy changes
evidence semantics or public outcome-label changes
provisional validation thresholds or high-confidence rule changes

aggregationPolicy.additiveClaimRequirement: A causal component may enter an additive caused-total only when every underlying resource or action has a stable unique claim reference and no claim reference appears in another additive component.
aggregationPolicy.overlapHandling: Outcome quantities may appear in explanatory views but verified outcomes are not caused totals. Direct marginal effects default to non-additive. Cooperative allocation is an alternative lens. Any additive causal aggregate requires unique claim references and must reject overlap.

shapleyPolicy.characteristicFunctionDefinition: For each eligible participant subset, coalition value is other eligible funding activated under the frozen threshold, deadline, payment, refund, and bonus rules, excluding unconditional funding and platform subsidies.
shapleyPolicy.approximationMethod: Above 10 participants, use deterministic seeded permutations and withhold when Monte Carlo error or coalition monotonicity diagnostics fail.

parameters.publicationRule: render deterministic terms and verified outcomes when valid; withhold every modeled causal component unless the exact active model has a current passing health snapshot
